pages.text: Yusuf (peace be upon him) saw a dream in his sleep, and told it to his father Ya'qub (peace be upon him).

Yusuf said to his father: ﴿يَـٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيۡتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوۡكَبٗا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ رَأَيۡتُهُمۡ لِي سَٰجِدِينَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'O my father, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them bowing down to me.' This dream was good news of the high rank he would reach.

His father advised him not to tell his dream to his brothers, lest they envy him and plot to destroy him, for Satan is a clear enemy to people. And he told him that his Lord would choose him, teach him the meaning of dreams, and complete His blessing upon him, as He completed it before upon his forefathers Ibrahim and Ishaq.

When Yusuf's brothers told him that their father had lost his sight from weeping over him, he sent his shirt with them, to cast it over his father's face so that his sight would return. And when the caravan set out with the shirt, Ya'qub told those around him that he could find the scent of Yusuf.

When the bearer of good news came, he cast the shirt over the face of Ya'qub, and he could see again. Ya'qub and his family set out for Egypt, and when they came in to Yusuf, he drew his parents close to him.

Yusuf raised his parents onto the throne, and they bowed down to him in greeting and honour, not in worship; that was allowed in their law, and it is forbidden in ours. And Yusuf said to his father: ﴿يَـٰٓأَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأۡوِيلُ رُءۡيَٰيَ مِن قَبۡلُ قَدۡ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي حَقّٗاۖ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'O my father, this is the meaning of my dream of before; my Lord has made it true.' Among the lessons of these verses: Allah is gentle in planning what He wills, all-knowing of what is good for His servants, wise in His words and deeds. And Ya'qub (peace be upon him) promised his sons to ask his Lord to forgive them when they admitted their wrong.
